mission.beneficiary: A developer who starts a coding agent on a Mac, leaves the desk, and needs to supervise, approve, recover, and collect the result safely from another device.
mission.consequential_choice: pivot: make controlled long-running coding-agent supervision the product boundary, retain raw terminal I/O only as an underlying transport and recovery escape hatch
falsifiers: Target developers consistently prefer unrestricted terminal access and do not value explicit run state, approvals, or completion handoffs.
The supported coding-agent workflows cannot expose reliable approval or completion signals without brittle terminal-output parsing.
Reconnect tests frequently create ambiguous ownership, duplicate input, missed approvals, or incorrect terminal states.
A controlled run cannot be made materially safer than raw terminal access while preserving a useful mobile workflow.
mission.interpretation: Generic remote terminal access leaves Termi competing on transport and terminal UX, while its persistence, relay, and policy foundations are better suited to supervising long-running coding agents. The product should own an agent-run lifecycle above tmux without pretending to own the underlying coding agent.
mission.mission: Pivot Termi into a controlled interface for long-running coding agents: let a user launch or adopt one run, safely leave and reconnect, review approval requests, and receive a clear completion or failure handoff from mobile or web.
mission.next_probe: Prototype one instrumented golden path around a single coding-agent session: create or adopt the run with one explicit owner, disconnect and reconnect, surface one confirm-required action, approve or deny it, then return a structured terminal state and summary. Test it across the connector and one remote client, recording every ownership ambiguity, lost event, and manual terminal escape.
non_goals: Building a general-purpose remote shell or full terminal emulator.
Replacing coding agents, tmux, or developers' existing local workflows.
Supporting multiple simultaneous controllers for one run.
Broadening platform coverage or adding terminal customization before the controlled run loop is validated.
Automatically approving consequential commands or promising unattended autonomy.
mission.rationale: This boundary turns existing terminal connectivity into a differentiated workflow and directly resolves the four required product questions. Termi should own the control record, authenticated viewers, approval state, reconnect semantics, and return summary; tmux should remain the execution substrate and raw terminal access should remain an escape hatch. A narrow end-to-end agent-run loop is more valuable now than expanding terminal features or maintaining equal investment across generic mobile and web terminal clients.
mission.situation: Termi already connects mobile and web clients to persistent tmux sessions through a macOS connector, with pairing, session discovery, live output, raw input, relay access, and an example command policy. Its current boundary is remote terminal I/O, while the unresolved product decision concerns ownership, reconnection, approvals, and how completed work returns to the user.
mission.success_signal: In repeated real runs, a developer can start or adopt a coding-agent session, disconnect, reconnect from mobile or web without losing run identity or duplicating control, resolve a gated approval, and receive an unambiguous completed, failed, or interrupted return state with a concise result summary.
